gaps: The `$!outputType()` dynamic object creation via substitute-variable syntax is a legacy PML1 construct not explicitly documented in KB syntax reference. Verified with lint — passes clean.
The `$!attributeName DEFAULT` syntax (legacy PML1 dollar-command form) is used in TryToSetValue but not documented in KB commands-reference. Verified with lint — passes clean.

gaps.name: using namespace with AVEVA internal objects
gaps.description: The pattern `using namespace 'RamAEUpdateElement'` followed by `object CREATEELEMENT()`, `object DELETEELEMENT()`, `object UPDATEATTRIBUTE()`, `object RECLASSIFYELEMENT()` is a project-specific .NET add-in integration pattern. KB has generic `using namespace` for .NET namespaces but not for AVEVA internal object factories.

gaps.name: var backref query syntax
gaps.description: The `var !backRefNoDetails backref(attname XRPNTR) of $!elementRefe` construct is a PDMS-specific query syntax for retrieving back-references. Not documented in KB loop/examples.

gaps.name: collectAllFor with WORL scope
gaps.description: The `!!collectAllFor(|UDA|, |UPCASE(UDNAME) EQ UPCASE('$!nameWithoutColon')|, WORL)` call uses the WORL scope for universal collection. KB has collectAllFor examples but not with WORL scope explicitly documented.

gaps.name: Pseudo attribute write access bypass
gaps.description: The `!attribute.isPseudo().not()` check in isAttributeUpdatable allows NAME attribute to bypass direct attribute check and proceed to element-level updatable check. This is a domain-specific logic not captured in KB.

gaps.name: XPI cross-reference validation
gaps.description: The isXpiItemUpdatable method traverses back-references to validate discipline-level updatable status. This distributed-element validation chain is complex and not covered in KB.

gaps.name: Dollar-substitute dynamic object creation
gaps.description: The pattern `object $!outputType()` creates a PML object dynamically from a type-name string. This is a legacy PML1 feature that works alongside PML2. Logic for when this is safe vs. unsafe is not documented in KB.

gaps.name: External object type RAMVALUECONVERTER
gaps.description: The object member `!this.valueConverter is RAMVALUECONVERTER` references an external class not defined in this file. KB has no entry for this custom converter pattern.

gaps.name: External object type RAMCOMMONLOGGER

gaps.name: RamAEUpdateElement namespace objects
gaps.description: CREATEELEMENT, DELETEELEMENT, UPDATEATTRIBUTE, RECLASSIFYELEMENT are .NET add-in objects from the RamAEUpdateElement namespace. KB has no entry for these specific AVEVA automation add-in objects.

newEntriesNeeded.title: Dynamic object construction via $! variable substitution
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The `$!varName` syntax substitutes a variable's value into command or expression text. When used as `object $!typeName()`, it dynamically creates an object of the type named by the variable's value. This is a PML1 legacy feature that coexists with PML2.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use `$!typeName` only when the type name is determined at runtime. Prefer direct `object TYPE()` when the type is known at compile time.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Dynamic object creation
!type = !currentValue.objecttype()
!output = object $!type()

-- Legacy PML1 dollar substitution in command context
$!attributeName DEFAULT
pitfalls: If the variable is UNSET or BADREF, the substitution produces empty string and the construct fails silently.
The substituted value is treated as a command/expression, not a type identifier, so type safety is not enforced.

newEntriesNeeded.title: PML var backref query for cross-references
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The `var` keyword with query clauses (e.g., `backref(attname ...) of $!obj`) creates a query variable that traverses AVEVA database relationships. This is a PDMS/E3D-specific query mechanism.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Always check `.set()` on var query results before accessing the variable value.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
var !queryVar queryClause of $!targetObject
if(!queryVar.set()) then
  -- process results
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Get back-references via XRPNTR attribute
var !backRefNoDetails backref(attname XRPNTR) of $!elementRefe
if(!backRefNoDetails.set()) then
  !backRefNos = !backRefNoDetails.split()
  do !backRefNo values !backRefNos
    !backRefe = !backRefNo.dbref()
    -- process back-reference
  enddo
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Missing .set() check
var !backRefNoDetails backref(attname XRPNTR) of $!elementRefe
!value = !backRefNoDetails -- may be BADREF
pitfalls: The `of $!targetObject` requires the target to resolve to a valid reference.
The query result may be UNSET if no back-references exist.
Split results need individual dbref() conversion.

newEntriesNeeded.title: AVEVA automation add-in namespace objects
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The `using namespace 'ModuleName'` directive allows creating objects from .NET add-in assemblies. AVEVA provides internal namespaces like RamAEUpdateElement with factory objects (CREATEELEMENT, DELETEELEMENT, UPDATEATTRIBUTE, RECLASSIFYELEMENT).
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Always wrap namespace object creation in handle/elsehandle blocks since .NET objects may throw exceptions.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
using namespace 'NamespaceName'
!obj = object OBJECTNAME()
handle any
  -- error handling
elsehandle none
  -- success
endhandle
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
using namespace 'RamAEUpdateElement'
!elementNet = object CREATEELEMENT()
!elementNet.setElementTypeByName('|$!<type>|')
handle any
  !this.addErrorToList(!name, 'NAME', !!error.text)
elsehandle none
  !elementNet.addAttributeValue(|NAME|, !validName)
  !elementNet.executeSync()
endhandle
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- No error handling on .NET object creation
!obj = object CREATEELEMENT()
!obj.executeSync() -- may throw
pitfalls: The namespace must be imported/available at runtime.
.NET objects may throw exceptions not caught by PML's handle any unless explicitly wrapped.
Some namespace objects require specific execution order (e.g., setElementType before execute).

newEntriesNeeded.title: collectAllFor with WORL scope for universal search
newEntriesNeeded.principle: The `!!collectAllFor(type, expression, scope)` function searches the AVEVA database for elements matching criteria. The WORL scope searches universally across all disciplines.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Always check `.set()` on the result before accessing `.first()` or iterating.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- Find UDA by name universally
!udaList = !!collectAllFor(|UDA|, |UPCASE(UDNAME) EQ UPCASE('MyUDA')|, WORL)
if(!udaList.set()) then
  !attributeRefe = !udaList.first()
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- No set() check
!udaList = !!collectAllFor(|UDA|, |EXPRESSION|, WORL)
!target = !udaList.first() -- may fail if empty
pitfalls: WORL scope can be slow on large projects.
Expression syntax depends on AVEVA product version.
Result may be empty if no matching elements exist.

newEntriesNeeded.title: Pseudo attribute write access bypass in AVEVA
newEntriesNeeded.principle: Some AVEVA attributes (like NAME) are marked as pseudo-attributes that have special write access rules. The `isPseudo()` check allows bypassing direct attribute membership checks for these special attributes.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Always combine `isPseudo()` checks with `EQNoCase('NAME')` for NAME attribute special handling.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
!attribute = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName)
if(!attribute.isPseudo().not() OR !attributeName.EQNoCase('NAME')) then
  -- special handling for pseudo/NAME attributes
else
  !directAttributes = !elementRefe.attributes()
  -- normal attribute check
endif
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
define method .isAttributeUpdatable(!elementRefe is DBREF, !attributeName is STRING) is BOOLEAN
  !isUpdatable = false
  !attribute = object ATTRIBUTE(!attributeName)
  if(!attribute.isPseudo().not() OR !attributeName.EQNoCase('NAME')) then
    !isUpdatable = !this.isElementUpdatable(!elementRefe)
  else
    !directAttributes = !elementRefe.attributes()
    !isDirectAttribute = !directAttributes.findFirst(!attributeName.upcase()).set()
    if(!isDirectAttribute) then
      !isUpdatable = !this.isElementUpdatable(!elementRefe)
    endif
  endif
  return !isUpdatable
endmethod
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- Missing pseudo check
!directAttributes = !elementRefe.attributes()
!isDirect = !directAttributes.findFirst(!attributeName).set()
-- NAME may pass even though not in directAttributes
pitfalls: NAME attribute is always pseudo but always updatable via element methods.
Other pseudo attributes may have different rules.
Distributed attributes bypass this check entirely.
